title: A ‘Doom Loop’ Threatens France as Populism Confronts Markets
partialText: The turmoil shows the profound challenges facing governments stuck between unhappy citizens and wary bond investors.

title: France to Extend Curfews After Calm Night Follows Days of Riots
partialText: The targeted restrictions are part of a state effort to reassert control after the country’s largest riots in years, as those arrested in the chaos face expedited trials.

title: Student Protesters in France Have a Strange New Slogan. What Does It Mean?
partialText: “Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres” has appeared on signs at recent demonstrations. It doesn’t make much sense (it means, “In the name of God, it’s the darkness”) but is seen as shorthand for a generational divide.

title: Heading to France? Amid Recent Unrest, Here’s What to Know
partialText: Rioting over affordability and public education has swept through Paris and other French cities, and there may be more to come.

title: James Talarico on the Rage Economy, Billionaires and Flipping Texas
partialText: Our interview with James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Texas.

title: Why Zelensky Took the Gloves Off This Time With Trump
partialText: Staying quiet is riskier than speaking up, Ukrainian officials say, as President Trump goes further than ever in prioritizing Russia’s interests.

title: When Idaho Banned Abortion, OB-GYNs Fled. The Doctors Who Stayed Are Cracking.
partialText: From childbirth to miscarriages, women’s health care in the state has become increasingly dangerous.

title: Houdini Died on Halloween 100 Years Ago. Some Still Question How.
partialText: A urologist’s inquiry into the magician’s final days is the latest effort to grapple with outstanding questions about his demise.

title: Cornell’s Jane Doe Sent Letter to Faculty Senate Ahead of Vote
partialText: In a letter, the former student said she felt “unsupported” after hearing about an exchange between the school president and her sorority sister. Officials disputed her account of the conversation.

title: Trump’s D.C. Golf Course Renovation Plan Has Many Residents Feeling Discouraged
partialText: At East Potomac Park, several residents bemoaned a plan to revamp the federal property that might wipe out features they have cherished for years.

title: As Private Equity Scales Up Small Restaurants, Customers Push Back
partialText: Deep-pocketed investment groups are giving mom-and-pop food businesses a shot at big success. But many of their regulars are speaking out against those deals.

title: Yemeni City of Taiz Running Out of Essentials as Houthis Close in
partialText: The Iranian-backed Houthi militia has cut road access to Taiz, one of Yemen’s largest cities, besieging it. Officials there warn of an impending humanitarian disaster.

title: UK to Send Fighter Jets to Help Defend Saudi Arabia From Houthi Attacks
partialText: R.A.F. Typhoon fighter jets will be deployed to protect infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, Britain said, after a spike in attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi militia.

title: Why Does Saudi Arabia Struggle to Stop Houthi Attacks?
partialText: The Saudi military has expensive equipment, but the missiles and drones used by the Yemeni militia are difficult to detect and stop.

title: Knicks Ticket Prices Are Soaring After Last Season’s Championship
partialText: Knicks tickets have never been cheap, but prices for the first game alone are soaring after last season’s championship — more than a trip to Paris.

title: Stop Appeasing Russia
partialText: The stakes in Ukraine are much larger than the fate of one nation.

title: The History We Lost When Trump Tore Down the East Wing
partialText: Mr. Trump appears to wish to be both president and first lady.

title: Alberta Voters Reject Leaving Canada in Referendum on Separatism
partialText: Residents of the province were asked if they wished to remain in Canada or to hold another vote on breaking away, in a referendum that was a win for Prime Minister Mark Carney.
